products.name: Weekly Focus Planner
products.description: An undated productivity planning pack designed to help individuals organize their week, identify daily priorities, track habits, and review progress. Instant digital delivery. No physical item will be shipped.
products.short: An undated printable planner: a weekly plan, a daily priorities page, a monthly habit tracker and a weekly review.
products.format: Printable PDF in A4 and US Letter
includes: Instructions for printing and using the pages
goodFor: You like planning on paper, or writing on PDFs with a tablet and stylus.
You want a short weekly routine: plan on Monday, three priorities a day, review on Friday.
You'd rather print what you need than commit to a dated planner.
notFor: You want reminders, notifications or a calendar that syncs. These are printable pages, not an app.
You need to track projects with several people. The Project Workflow Bundle adds spreadsheets for that.

seo.title: Weekly Focus Planner: Undated Printable Weekly Planner (PDF)
seo.description: Undated printable weekly planner PDF with a daily priorities and task list, monthly habit tracker and weekly review. A4 and US Letter. $12.99 USD, one-time payment, digital download.

pages: How to use and print this planner
A simple weekly routine, what to print and how many copies, and printing tips.
Your focus, top three outcomes, deadlines and a box for each day of the week.
Three priorities, a task list with checkboxes, an hour-by-hour schedule and an end-of-day note.
Up to 12 habits across a month of 31 days, with a goal and a total for each (landscape page).
What got done, what slipped, wins, lessons, three 1-to-5 ratings and next week's top three.
A dot-grid page for notes, lists or sketches.

printables: An undated month grid with space for the month's projects, key deadlines and notes. Landscape.
Rows for tasks and milestones with owner, start and due dates, and 12 week columns to shade in. Landscape.
Fifteen steps in five groups (capture, clarify, organize, plan, review) with tick boxes for six weeks, so one printout lasts six weeks.

spreadsheets.name: Project tracker
sheets: Up to 30 projects with owner, status, priority, start and due dates. Calculates task counts, progress, days left and a health flag (on track, due soon, overdue, done).
Up to 300 tasks, each linked to a project from a drop-down list, with owner, status, priority, dates and an overdue flag.
A 26-week bar chart built from each project's start and due dates. The current week is shaded.
A calendar for any month showing open tasks due each day and the first project due, plus monthly counts.
The 15-step weekly routine with a column per week to tick off.
The options in the drop-down lists. Add your team's names here.

spreadsheets.name: Content calendar
sheets: Up to 400 planned items with publish date, channel, title, format, status, owner, draft due date and link. Flags past dates, late drafts and items due within 3 days.
A calendar for any month showing what's planned each day.
A list for ideas that don't have a date yet.
Channels, formats, statuses and people for the drop-down lists.

goodFor: Freelancers juggling several clients or projects at once.
Small teams that want one shared tracker without paying for project-management software.
Anyone planning a regular newsletter, blog or social media schedule.
notFor: Teams that need real-time collaboration, permissions or automatic reminders. A dedicated project-management app will suit you better.
People who only want to plan their own week on paper. The Weekly Focus Planner on its own costs less.
